reviewContext.note: RE-review focused on the sprint-1/2 demand that dseq/bid/lease parses be verified against REAL provider-services output. The captured real-chain evidence (2026-06-27-real-sandbox2-e2e.md) is treated as ground truth; the impl was checked to AGREE with it line by line. The three previously-blocking parse findings (FIND-001 dseq event-attr, FIND-002 .bid.id, lease state) are now corrected to the captured reality and the fake is non-circular. Two NEW/persisting defects keep the verdict at FAIL: a remaining --gas auto simulation that contradicts the spec's 'fixed gas' acceleration fix, and the absence of any behavioral test for the send-manifest fail-closed path that the evidence proves is the real-sandbox outcome.

evidence.description: dseq parse `select(.type=="akash.deployment.v1.EventDeploymentCreated")|.attributes[]?|select(.key=="id")|(.value|fromjson).dseq` EXACTLY matches evidence lines 15-18. No residual `select(.key=="dseq")` (grep-confirmed: select(.key== appears only at line 81 with =="id").

bid_id path `.[0].bid.id` (then .gseq/.oseq/.provider extracted from that id object) matches evidence line 19 (.bids[].bid.id {owner,dseq,gseq,oseq,provider,bseq}). No `.bid.bid_id` anywhere (grep-confirmed). `.bid.state=="open"` filter present (line 89).
Denom: SDL pricing default uact (41) + --deposit 5000000uact (77) per AEP-76 escrow; gas stays uakt (26). grep-confirmed uact only in pricing/deposit, uakt only in gas.

Fake jq-builds the EventDeploymentCreated `id` attribute as a JSON string ({owner,dseq:"777"}|tojson) — the real decoded shape. A regression to select(.key=="dseq") would find no such attribute -> empty DSEQ -> exit 1 -> happy-path assertion `OUT=777 && rc=0` (test:72-73) FAILS. Non-circular for dseq.

Fake bid emits `.bid.id` (not `.bid.bid_id`). A regression to `.bid.bid_id` yields null -> empty BID -> exit 1 'no open bids' -> happy-path assertion FAILS. gseq/oseq/provider are nested inside .bid.id matching the impl's extraction at line 95. Non-circular for bid_id.

Happy path asserts rc=0, OUT=777, and that deployment create / bid list / lease create / send-manifest were each actually invoked. Combined with the create/nobid/lease fail-closed cases (78-87), the oracle would catch a regression to any of the three wrong parses.

INV-1 (own-wallet --from, no console/credit-card/managed-wallet), INV-2 (cert<deploy<bid<lease<manifest ordered flow), INV-3 (no sleep 30, bid poll loop), INV-4 (cert only if none valid), INV-5 negative half (no mint/swap in active code), INV-6 (fail-closed exits) all hold. FAIL is driven by FIND-301: AKASH_GAS defaults to `auto` (line 26), keeping the --gas auto simulation the spec (line 43/54) requires removed via 'fixed gas'.

The dseq print (line 123) is reached only after create code==0, numeric dseq, bid found, provider present, lease code==0, lease active, and manifest sent. Every failure path exits 1 BEFORE line 123, so no dseq leaks on failure (HARD 0.24).
The three behavioral fail-closed cases (create code!=0, no bids, lease code!=0) still genuinely assert rc!=0 AND empty stdout AND no downstream call, and remain valid after the fake's shape changes.

Script prints ONLY the dseq, and only after lease-active (113) + send-manifest returned 0 (121). It never asserts a booted container. On the real sandbox-2 chain (evidence: providers 400 on send-manifest) the script would exit 1 at line 121 rather than overclaim. The 'child ACTUALLY boots' wording is a header comment (line 4), not a runtime claim.
Test does not assert a container boot; the fake returns send-manifest ok and the test only checks the dseq parse + ordered calls. No boot overclaim in the oracle.

FIND-302: the send-manifest fail-closed path (deploy-akash.sh:114-121) — which evidence line 22-23 proves is the actual sandbox-2 outcome (provider 400) — has NO behavioral test. mkfake has no `manifest` fail mode; *send-manifest* always echoes ok. The fail-closed guarantee for the most-likely real path is unverified.

FIND-002/FIND-202 (bid_id .bid.id, cheapest open) — now matches real shape, non-circular
